transcript.text: The first red day I was down $8,000. The
second red day I lost another 3,000.
Now, that's good in a way because what
sometimes happens is that you lose
progressively more and more and more.
You lose 8,000, then 16, then 32 because
you're getting into that mindset of I
want to try to make it all back in one
day, so you're taking more risk. And
obviously I lost on the second day
$3,000, but I made the good decision of
reducing my share size a little bit so
that the total amount of the loss would
be more manageable if I had another red
day cuz that's the thing. When you come
in each day, you don't know if it's
going to be a red day or green day, but
you can control how much you're willing
to risk. So, if it's red, the loss will
be manageable. And this is the idea is
to make sure you're never losing more
than you can tolerate.

metadata.title: DONT GET CAUGHT IN THIS RED DAY CYCLE!
